daily_summary.html:
Domestic Politics

Indonesia's national police have named former National Police Chief Listyo Sigit and two other senior officers as suspects in an illegal wiretapping operation targeting President Prabowo Subianto. The wiretapping allegedly began in 2025 while Listyo was still police chief, with targets including the president, ministers, and business figures. Listyo, who was appointed Presidential Chief of Staff just a month ago, has been detained at National Police headquarters and faces up to 10 years imprisonment.

  • DPR lawmakers have backed the police investigation into the presidential wiretapping scandal, while the government has urged public trust in the ongoing probe.
  • Former Coordinating Minister for Political, Legal and Security Affairs Mahfud MD called the wiretapping scandal "the worst crime in police history", describing it as shocking that a supposedly exemplary officer committed such acts.
  • A university professor warned that the prolonged controversy over Vice President Gibran's diploma is eroding the legitimacy of the Prabowo administration.
  • The Indonesian Legal Aid Foundation (YLBHI) has urged police to reveal who ordered the wiretapping operation against President Prabowo.
  • Gerindra party dismissed a party member over a drug party case and denied any intervention in the matter.
  • National Police Chief Suyudi has issued orders replacing 264 high-ranking officers in his fifth wave of personnel reshuffles.
  • Labor leader Said Iqbal has demanded guidance for determining the 2027 minimum wage increase.
  • A deputy social affairs minister announced that journalist Udin has been proposed as a national hero as a symbol of press freedom.

Foreign Policy & Defence

The Indonesian military has deployed 180 personnel to Central Africa for a United Nations peacekeeping mission. The TNI has also addressed the deployment of tens of thousands of marines to the Jakarta area, with its spokesman stating the forces are safeguarding national unity.

  • State holding company Danantara is preparing a project pipeline for talks with the United States ahead of the G20 summit.
  • An Indonesian youth delegation has explored ancient architecture and cultural heritage sites in Shanxi, China.
  • Indonesian Nusantara coffee attracted visitors at the Swiss Coffee Festival 2026.
  • The Council of Indonesian Ulama (MUI) has met with Egypt's Minister of Endowments, Dar Al-Ifta, and Al-Azhar to build a global Islamic alliance.

Other

The Financial System Stability Committee (KSSK) has revised Indonesia's 2026 economic growth projection to 5.4-5.5 percent. The rupiah gained 0.15 percent to 18,132 per US dollar, while the government is planning to boost rupiah conversion of export earnings to strengthen the currency.

  • Finance Minister Sri Mulyani has affirmed that interbank transfers and digital wallet transactions are exempt from value-added tax.
  • An Indonesian lawmaker is seeking a review of VAT imposed on menstrual products.
  • Indonesia held its first Patent Business Forum to boost commercialization of intellectual property.
  • The Free Nutritious Meals Agency (BGN) has capped kitchen operational costs at Rp 3,000 per recipient, with oversight being strengthened by appointing former KPK officials.
  • Public Works Minister has ordered assessment of damage from Semeru volcano lahar floods, while Home Affairs Minister Tito visited Pidie Jaya to inspect flood-damaged embankments.
  • Indonesian railway company KAI has added stops for long-distance trains at Bekasi, Cikarang, and Jatinegara stations.
